sections.title: Configuration Basics
sections.text:
4.1 Configuration Basics
Let’s begin with a configuration check to ensure that the material type-related settings
are in place in SAP S/4HANA so that you can successfully integrate QM with MM.

sections.title: Material Type/Task List Combination
sections.text:
4.1.1 Material Type/Task List Combination
If the company uses the standard material types, such as raw materials (ROH), finished
goods (FERT), or trading goods (HAWA), then their task list types are available in the
system. However, if any material type that you want to go through the quality inspec-
tion and control process (e.g., spare parts [ERSA] or a company-specific material type)
isn’t available, then you need to ensure that the combination of task list type Q with the
material type exists in the system. To do so, follow configuration menu path SAP IMG 
Quality Management  QM Planning  Inspection Planning  Assign Task List Type to
Material Type. Choose New Entries, add the material type/task list type combination,
and then save your entries.

sections.title: Control Key for Quality Management in Procurement

4.1.2 Control Key for Quality Management in Procurement
The QM control key plays a crucial role in meeting the business needs of a company.
For example, using control keys in procurement, you can block supplier payments or
all supplier activities until delivered goods clear the quality control process. After mak-
ing the necessary configuration settings for the QM control key, you need to assign it
in the QM view of the material master, which we’ll cover in Section 4.2.1.
To define a QM control key, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  QM in
Logistics  QM in Procurement  Define Control Keys. Choose QM Control Key “0007”,

4.2 Procurement Business Processes
Let’s now delve into the various business processes of procurement and IM. Each sec-
tion will provide an overview of the integrated QM and MM business processes, detail
the master data checklist, and then provide more details.

sections.title: Goods Receipt in Procurement: Inspection Type 01
sections.text:
4.2.1 Goods Receipt in Procurement: Inspection Type 01
Figure 4.3 shows a commonly used business process in which a standard procurement
process integrates with QM. This process begins with creating a purchase order for a
supplier to deliver the material. As soon as the company records the goods receipt with
reference to the purchase order, the system creates an inspection lot. Standard QM pro-
cesses, such as results recording, occur, followed by usage decisions and stock posting.
On quality clearance of goods, the supplier submits the invoice for payment.
Figure 4.3 QM Integration into Procurement Process
In the next sections, you’ll either set up the master data required for this business pro-
cess or check that the relevant master data exists. Upon ensuring master data availabil-
ity, you’ll see impacts of configuration and master data setup on business processes.

As soon as you record the goods receipt for a purchase order, the system creates both a

sections.title: Source Inspection: Inspection Type 0101
sections.text:
4.2.2 Source Inspection: Inspection Type 0101
Source inspection in QM ensures that the quality of procured goods is checked and
approved for compliance before the supplier delivers the goods at the company’s ware-
house. In source inspection, the supplier can then immediately deal with any defects in a
product’s quality. The company can use this functionality to track when source inspec-
tion needs to occur and carry it out. This saves the time that otherwise would be lost if the
defective goods were delivered by the supplier and rejected (or asked to be reworked) by
the company. You can quickly set up source inspection functionality to bring about sig-
nificant overall process improvements and optimization to reduce the overall lead time
incurred in ensuring that only quality goods are delivered by the supplier.
You can implement source inspection at any time, even after an SAP S/4HANA system
and the QM functionality are already implemented in a company. The option to inte-
grate source inspection in the procurement process can be part of ongoing improve-
ments and optimization in business processes in general and the procurement process
in particular.
For source inspection, create a purchase order so that you can see the importance of
the delivery date and how source inspection takes it into account. Then, create an
inspection lot by manually triggering the source inspection program. Record the
results and make a usage decision about the goods by rejecting them, so that on goods
receipt from the supplier and against the same purchase order, the system creates a
new inspection lot. All of these settings are the direct result of configuration settings
that we made in QM Control Key (see Figure 4.12).
Figure 4.12 Source Inspection in Procurement Process
Let’s go over these processes in detail in the following sections.
QM Master Data Checklist
The following is the QM master data checklist:
 Inspection type 0101 active in QM view of material master
 Quality information record: procurement
 Inspection plan usage 51 and status 4 (for released)
Next, we’ll go through the process of creating a purchase order, followed by manually
triggering the source inspection that results in the creation of the inspection lot.

sections.title: First Article Inspection for Production Part Approval Process
sections.text:
4.3 First Article Inspection for Production Part Approval Process
The remaining QM business processes for source inspection are the same:
 Record results for source inspection (Transaction QE01)
 Usage decision (Transaction QA11)
Invoice Receipt
The business process of the invoice receipt is the same as we previously covered in Sec-
tion 4.2.1.
4.3 First Article Inspection for Production Part Approval Process
SAP has introduced first article inspection for the production part approval process to
cater to the quality control and quality assurance needs of industries, such as automo-
tive, aerospace, and so on to ensure comprehensive pre-inspection of underproduction
products by a company. It’s an alternate to pilot run inspection, which we’ll discuss in
Section 4.4. A model inspection is used to identify and rectify quality issues beforehand
prior to the production of remaining products. The first article inspection for the pro-
duction part approval process is a new feature in SAP S/4HANA and can be easily set up
as long as the necessary configuration, master data, and business processes are put in
place that enable effectively reporting for timely and informed business decisions. Once
the supplier has passed the quality process of first article inspection for the production
part approval process for the material to be supplied to the company, then the regular
quality inspection can take place. As needed, first article inspection for the production
part approval process can also be reinitiated to begin the reevaluation of a supplier.
Figure 4.18 shows the end-to-end business processes for first article inspection for pro-
duction part approval. In the business process, the first step is to make the relevant set-
ting in the quality info record, which is relevant for first article approval for production
part approval. This is then followed by the regular procure-to-pay process (purchase to
goods receipt), and the goods receipt will generate an inspection lot of type 01 (goods
receipt inspection for purchase order) associated to standard inspection plan usage 51
(goods receipt model inspection).
Figure 4.18 Business Process of First Article Inspection for the Production Part
Approval Process

inspection for the production part approval process:

sections.title: Pilot Run Inspection: Inspection Type 0102
sections.text:
4.4 Pilot Run Inspection: Inspection Type 0102
Before “upgrading” the status of a first-time or new supplier to that of a regular sup-
plier, a company often has stringent and comprehensive procedures and processes in
place to ensure that a new supplier is able to provide material of sufficient quality. To
achieve this objective, the company makes the supplier go through a series of trial runs
or pilot runs of materials until the supplier is able to fulfill the quality requirements.
Here, the SAP system can help by enabling the procurement and quality planners to
put a series of checks and controls in place via status management. With each mate-
rial’s delivery from the supplier, its corresponding inspection lot creation, results
recording, and usage decision update the status (and controls) for the supplier.
The following sections begin with discussing the necessary configuration settings that
need to be in place for pilot run inspection so the same can then be assigned in the mas-
ter data. The master data is then used to discuss the business processes of pilot run
inspection.

sections.title: Configuration Basics
sections.text:
4.4.1 Configuration Basics
Before we cover the configuration basics of the pilot run, see Figure 4.25, which shows
the Status tab of the quality info record (Transaction QI01), in which we assigned Status
Profile QM_P_001. A status profile controls various business functions and whether
they are allowed. A status profile is a cross-application component, so you can use it to
control business functions not just in the QM area but also in other logistics and supply
chain management areas.
Figure 4.25 Status Profile in the Quality Info Record
© 

259
4.4 Pilot Run Inspection: Inspection Type 0102
In this example of a pilot run inspection, use status profile QM_P_001, which SAP
delivers. Alternatively, you can amend an existing status profile or create a new one
with menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Quality in Logistics  QM in Procure-
ment  Define Status of Supply Relationships.
Figure 4.26 shows the standard supplier relationship status profile QM_P_001 available
in the system. Here, there are multiple statuses, and the initial status is 0001 (Supply
Relationship Initiated). The initial status is denoted by the checkbox selected in the Init.
status column. The low and high numbers of the status control how the system
changes from one status to another.
Figure 4.26 Status Profile
Figure 4.27 shows the assignment of different statuses of status profile QM_P_001 to
inspection lots. To assign statuses to inspection types so that the system is able to fol-
low the sequence in creating various inspection types, follow menu path SAP IMG 
Quality Management  Quality in Logistics  QM in Procurement  Maintain Inspection
Lot Origins & Assign Inspection Types.
For this example, choose three different statuses of status profile QM_P_001, and cor-
respondingly assign three different inspection types: 0101, 0102, and 01. When the sys-
tem receives the material from the supplier and against the purchase order, it creates
an inspection lot of inspection type 0101. This is because you assigned status 0002 to
inspection type 0101, and this is the first status among the three statuses. On accepted
usage decision for this inspection lot (and of inspection type 0101), the system auto-
matically switches to the next status, which is 0003 (and correspondingly having
inspection type 0102; look for the Next status column in Figure 4.27 to see how status
change works).

4 Integrating with Materials Management
260
Figure 4.27 Status Profile and Assignment to Inspection Types
In Section 4.4.3, we’ll cover end-to-end business processes of all three inspection types
and their statuses.
Tips and Tricks
If you’ve configured other specific inspection types to attend to the pilot run inspec-
tion’s business scenario, you can assign these configured inspection types at this stage
(Figure 4.27).

sections.title: Business Processes of Pilot Run Inspection
sections.text:
4.4.3 Business Processes of Pilot Run Inspection
In this business process, the first step is to create a purchase order for new a supplier and
partially or completely receive goods. The system creates an inspection lot of inspection
type 0101. Perform results recording, followed by making a usage decision and stock
posting. The system considers the usage decision at this stage to decide whether it
should move to the next status or remain the same. An accepted usage decision for
inspection type 0101 triggers the system to create the inspection lot of inspection type
0102, and on the next goods receipt against the same purchase order or even a different
purchase order. Again, the system considers results recorded and usage decision taken
for the inspection lot of inspection type 0102 to see if it should switch the status to
inspection type 01 or not. Finally, the accepted usage decision of inspection type 0102
© 

261
4.4 Pilot Run Inspection: Inspection Type 0102
leads to the system updating to inspection type 01. You then pay the supplier for goods
delivered. The business process of the pilot run inspection is shown in Figure 4.28.
Figure 4.28 Business Processes in Model Inspection
Create a purchase order using Transaction ME21N; in this example, the system creates
purchase order number 4500001848. On goods receipt against the purchase order

4.5 Subcontracting: Inspection Type 0130
The subcontracting process begins when the company hands over (issues) the compo-
nents to a subcontractor, who is usually a supplier, against the subcontracting pur-
chase order, to either assemble or add value to the product. The company takes the
components’ inventory out of its books, and the same is reflected in the supplier’s
inventory. When the supplier has done what it’s contracted to do, the company
receives the goods against the same subcontracting purchase order from the supplier.
On goods receipt from external processing (subcontracting), the system creates an
inspection lot of inspection type 0130. Figure 4.33 shows the end-to-end subcontract-
ing business process. The supplier invoices the company for the services rendered and
receives payment.
Figure 4.33 Subcontracting Business Process
The following sections discuss the QM master data checklist to ensure that relevant
QM master data is already created, as well as the end-to-end subcontracting process,
which also involves quality inspection of externally processed material (subcon-
tracted material).

4.6.1 Stock Transfer Inspection: Inspection Type 08
Components procured or produced in one plant may be required for assembly or con-
sumption in another plant, which requires a stock transfer. In the quality inspection
business process of stock transfers, it’s possible to conduct a quality inspection process
not just for interplant or plant-to-plant stock transfer but also for other inventory man-
agement functions, such as for store-to-store stock transfer within the same plant and
material-to-material stock transfer. In this example, we’ll cover interplant transfer
posting—that is, plant-to-plant stock transfer using a stock transport order.
For a stock transport order for interplant transfer, the following sequence of steps is
involved:
1 Create a stock transport order that consists of supplying plant and receiving plant
details, along with other materials and quantities.
2 Goods are issued from the supplying plant with reference to the stock transport
order. These goods are shown as stock in transit.
3 Goods are received at the receiving plant with reference to the same stock transport
order.
4 Upon goods receipt at the receiving plant, the system creates an inspection lot for
interplant stock transfer.
Figure 4.39 shows the end-to-end business process of a stock transport order and for
stock transfer between two plants.

4.6.2 Other Goods Receipt: Inspection Type 05
Although it may not happen all that frequently, companies also face or have business
needs for which it’s imperative to quickly procure, receive, and make available goods
for further consumption. This may be the case when, due to the urgency of a material
requirement, a procurement person places and receives a material without going
through the standard procurement process. On goods receipt without reference to a
purchase order, the system still asks for supplier details to book its payment liability
and be able to pay for the procured goods. For such business processes, SAP S/4HANA
offers a standard inspection type to ensure that material received without reference to
a purchase order still gets inspected.

4 Integrating with Materials Management
274
The following sections discuss the QM master data checklist to ensure the same is cre-
ated and available in the system before proceeding further with discussion of the busi-
ness process of goods receipt without a purchase order, which triggers the quality
inspection process.
QM Master Data Checklist
The following is the QM master data checklist that you need to ensure:
 Inspection type 05 active in the QM view of the material master
 Inspection plan usage 5 and status 4 (for released)
Goods Receipt without Purchase Order
Access the screen in Figure 4.45 via Transaction MIGO, and select Goods Receipt and
then Other from the dropdown lists at the top. The movement type for goods receipt
without referring to a purchase order is 501 as shown on the far-right side of the screen.
You need to enter the material code, its quantity, plant, storage location, and the sup-
plier who delivered the material. If it’s a batch-managed material, then the system will
create a batch number. Save your entries. Figure 4.45 shows the material document cre-
ated as the result of goods receipt without reference to a purchase order.
Figure 4.45 Other Goods Receipt
Figure 4.46 shows the inspection lot (Transaction QA03) that the system creates on
goods receipt and without referring to any purchase order. The inspection type is 05
and consists of all the relevant details that the system created in the previous step. It
also consists of the material document details of goods receipt.

4.7 Handling Inspection Stock at QM Activation: Inspection Type 0800
Figure 4.46 Inspection Lot of Inspection Type 05
4.7 Handling Inspection Stock at QM Activation: Inspection
Type 0800
You can integrate QM even after implementation of SAP’s core business processes such
as in areas of MM, SAP S/4HANA Sales, production planning (PP), finance, and con-
trolling. Until then, the only limited option available to restrict a material’s free-to-use
stock (aka unrestricted stock) is to transfer or receive the stock as quality inspection
stock. On quality clearance (out of SAP) from the quality department, the user performs
the transfer posting of quality inspection stock to unrestricted-use stock by using
Transaction MIGO and movement type 321.
When the company implements QM and integrates it in logistics areas, the system
requires that all stock placed in quality inspection within MM and not QM undergoes
quality inspection again. This activity prevents inconsistencies between the stocks
placed in quality inspection within MM and the stock that requires handling in QM. To
attend to this scenario of ensuring stock consistency upon integrating QM with logis-
tics, SAP S/4HANA offers standard inspection type 0800.

4 Integrating with Materials Management
276
However, to use inspection type 0800, you need to ensure that a single configuration
setting is in place and then run its business process. Let’s first cover the configuration
settings that you need to activate to use inspection type 0800.

sections.title: Configuration Settings
sections.text:
4.7.1 Configuration Settings
At the plant level, you need to assign inspection type 0800 to each of the plants in
which you plan to integrate QM. For this example, use plant 1710, and assign inspection
type 0800. To perform the necessary configuration setting, follow menu path SAP IMG 
Quality Management  Basic Settings  Maintain Settings at Plant Level. Choose Plant
1710, and enter “0800” in the InspTypeforInspStock field in the Insp. lot creation tab.
Save your settings.

sections.text:
4.8 Summary
Tips and Tricks
If you don’t want to use inspection type 08 in your routine business processes, you can
also use Transaction QA08 to deactivate inspection type 08 using the options available
in the Deactivate Inspection Type tab shown earlier in Figure 4.48.
Figure 4.51 shows the display inspection lot (using Transaction QA03) of inspection lot
80000000456. The inspection type that the system assigns is 0800.
Note
You now have a good understanding of how QM integrates with MM and how inspec-
tion types (and inspection origins) relate to movement types in SAP. In Appendix A,
you’ll find a selected list movement types and associated inspection origins. You can
use that list to integrate QM into many more business processes of procurement and
inventory management as deemed necessary to meet business needs.
4.8 Summary
In this chapter, you’ve seen how standard configurations and functionalities offered by
SAP are sufficient to integrate QM into procurement and inventory management pro-
cesses.
The QM master data plays a central role in the effective implementation of QM in the
procurement and inventory management processes. This one-time setup requires sig-
nificant planning and concerted efforts, the importance of which can’t be overempha-
sized.
Apart from the routine procurement and inventory management processes in which
you can integrate QM functionality, the SAP system also offers several options to man-
age the complex and diverse businesses processes involved in the entire supply chain
and logistics functions. Some of these are subcontracting, stock transfer, and goods
receipt without reference to any procurement element, and you can integrate QM in all
these business processes.
The next chapter covers QM integration into production processes.
